fightLines.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Debbie Friedrich. Infantry soldier. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dispatcher's headset, Mixtape, Dog tags, Trail compass, Seed packet. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
You remember the Hunting spear at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Camo Jacket at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.

◈ FLASHBACK — Trail compass
Lost above the fog line, visibility down to your boots. You didn't panic — just held the compass flat, found north, and walked out like it was nothing. It was not nothing.
It sits up on its hind legs — hands moving too fast to follow. It's not looking at you. It's looking at your pack.
It circles once, eyes never leaving your pack — those hands never stop moving.

◈ RESONANCE HARMONICS — SYSTEM: "HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. Objects with high observer-attention waveforms function as auxiliary capacitors. We call this RESONANCE HARMONICS. We do not know why the waveforms taste like grief. We have stopped asking." — Hold a keepsake. Think about them. The System will do the math. (It is not math. It is love. The System will never know.) Channel keepsakes from your pack.
